findings.title: Session closure reason is required by SPEC-00 but has no schema field or repository API
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam C and §6 Glossary; SPEC-04 §3 schema; SPEC-04 §6.2
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 Seam C: "On session closure ... SPEC-04 records a session-closure event noting the reason." SPEC-00 §6 Glossary defines closure reasons `explicit_shutdown`, `superseded_session`, `heartbeat_timeout`. SPEC-04 `dhf.sessions` schema contains `started_at` and `ended_at` but no closure-reason column, and `CloseSessionAsync(Guid sessionId, CancellationToken ct)` only executes `UPDATE dhf.sessions SET ended_at = NOW()`.
findings.problem: The specs require durable recording of closure reason, but the database schema and write API cannot store it.
findings.why_it_matters: This cannot be implemented or acceptance-tested as written, and downstream session-recovery logic depends on distinguishing closure causes.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a persisted `closure_reason` field (and any needed metadata) to `dhf.sessions`, thread it through `CloseSessionAsync`/session-split paths, expose it in read DTOs, and update tests; or explicitly downgrade closure reason to log-only in every spec.

findings.title: SPEC-04 defines contradictory entry hash inputs
findings.evidence: SPEC-04 §4.2 `DhfHashColumns` includes `"entry_id", "session_id", "sequence_number"`. SPEC-04 §4.2a says those same columns are "NOT included in DhfHashColumns".
findings.problem: The writer and validator cannot share a single authoritative hash contract because the spec simultaneously includes and excludes the same fields.
findings.why_it_matters: Hash generation and deep validation will diverge immediately, breaking chain verification and making persisted hashes unstable.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one authoritative hashed-column set, remove the conflicting statement, and align `DhfHashColumns`, validator logic, and sync tests to that single list.

findings.title: Mandatory viewer entries endpoint requests fields absent from the only read-only DTO it is allowed to use
findings.evidence: SPEC-06 §4.3 example for `GET /api/dhf/entries?sessionId={uuid}` includes `undoOutcome`, `recordHash`, and `previousHash`. SPEC-04 §9.2 defines `EntryListItem` as `(EntryId, SequenceNumber, Timestamp, InputModality, TurnType, RawTranscript, ToolCallCount, HasDecorations)`.
findings.problem: The mandatory endpoint contract cannot be produced from `IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ListEntriesAsync` without adding undeclared repository fields or a second projection path.
findings.why_it_matters: This creates immediate integration churn between SPEC-04 and SPEC-06 and blocks implementation of the endpoint as specified.
findings.proposed_fix: Either extend `EntryListItem` in SPEC-04 to include the required fields, or reduce the SPEC-06 response contract to the fields actually available from the read-only repository.

findings.title: v2 screenshot viewing path is not representable in the current read model
findings.evidence: Migration doc §3 v2: "DHF stores S3 key; viewer and Anthropic vision API fetch via the presigned GET URL." SPEC-04 read-side `EntryDetail` exposes only `byte[]? ScreenshotBeforePng` / `ScreenshotAfterPng`. SPEC-06 §5.2 says `screenshotBefore.dataUrl` is `data:image/png...` "or `https://...` presigned (v2)".
findings.problem: The read-only contract has no field for an S3 key or presigned URL, so the v2 viewer contract cannot be implemented without changing SPEC-04.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the stated "no rewrites between v1 and v2" goal and guarantees a cross-spec DTO change during migration.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a version-agnostic screenshot reference DTO now (e.g. bytes-or-url discriminator with optional key/hash metadata) and use it in SPEC-04 and SPEC-06.

findings.title: ACC identifiers 25-27 are assigned to different capabilities in SPEC-00 and SPEC-07
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 assigns `ACC-25`/`ACC-26`/`ACC-27` to durable session lock, recovery-event persistence, and neutral landing page. SPEC-07 §12 assigns `ACC-25`/`ACC-26`/`ACC-27` to multi-domain resolution, decoration-write durability, and bouncer-cache behavior.
findings.problem: The same acceptance-test IDs refer to different requirements across specs.
findings.why_it_matters: CI reporting, traceability, and never-descopable gate enforcement become ambiguous and cannot be automated reliably.
findings.proposed_fix: Renumber SPEC-07 acceptance tests or update the SPEC-00 master table and all downstream references so every ACC ID is globally unique.

findings.title: SPEC-01 contradicts itself on whether ProtocolVersion mismatch can be detected during HTTP upgrade
findings.evidence: SPEC-01 §10: "Add-in sends `AddinReadyMessage` with `ProtocolVersion = Current` ... Mismatch → orchestrator sends a version-mismatch error ... then closes the WebSocket." SPEC-01 §9.1 m4: "It is caught by §10's version-mismatch handling (HTTP 400 during HTTP upgrade or close code 1002 during WebSocket protocol-error handling)".
findings.problem: ProtocolVersion is carried in `AddinReadyMessage`, which is sent after upgrade, so the documented HTTP-400-on-upgrade path is impossible.
findings.why_it_matters: Reconnect and regeneration logic depends on which transport signal occurs; contradictory behavior here will cause mismatched client/server implementations.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the HTTP-upgrade variant and define one post-upgrade version-mismatch path, including exact error message and close behavior.

findings.title: Locked-session recovery runbook is inconsistent across specs
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam C and §6 Glossary; SPEC-04 migration 008 comments; SPEC-04 §6.4
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 Seam C: "operator unlocks the session via SQL ... and starts a new session." SPEC-00 §6 Glossary: "manual SQL unlock is required to resume." SPEC-04 migration 008 says the trigger rejects `locked_at` non-NULL→NULL, recommends closing the session and starting a new one, and treats trigger bypass as last resort.
findings.problem: The operational procedure for a locked session is internally inconsistent: one spec requires supported SQL unlock/resume, another explicitly blocks unlock and recommends close-and-restart.
findings.why_it_matters: Incident response, lifecycle handling, and acceptance tests for locked sessions cannot be implemented consistently.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one supported recovery model—either a real unlock path with schema/API support, or close-and-new-session only—and align SPEC-00, SPEC-04, tests, and user messaging to that single path.

top_3_must_fix: Add a persisted session closure-reason contract or remove all claims that closure reasons are recorded in DHF.
Resolve the SPEC-04 hash-input contradiction so writers and validators use one identical `DhfHashColumns` definition.
Align SPEC-06 mandatory endpoint payloads with SPEC-04 read-only DTOs, including the v2 screenshot reference model.
